If 1 is entered for &acirc;&euro;&oelig;none&acirc;&euro;, no other entries should be made against any other fields pertaining to disability categories. Children may have multiple disabilities, in which case more than one category can be entered as true. There may be a small number of children who are disabled, but do not have any of the specified disabilities. For these children, &acirc;&euro;&oelig;none&acirc;&euro; should be 0 and each of the specified disability types should also be 0.

Column Description: A True/False field indicating whether the child&#039;s immunisations were up-to-date on 31 March 20XX. For the purposes of the CRCS census &acirc;&euro;&tilde;up to date&acirc;&euro;&trade; means that by 31 March 20XX the child has had all the immunisations that a child of their age should have received according to the current information on Scheduled Childhood Immunisations found on the Public Health Wales website. It is not a requirement of this question that the child received the immunisations strictly at the ages set out in the table, but merely that by 31 March the child&acirc;&euro;&trade;s immunisations had been brought &acirc;&euro;&tilde;up to date&acirc;&euro;&trade;, even if they were given late according to the immunisation timetable. In cases where children have not received their immunisations because of parental refusal, for health reasons, or because the young person refuses, they should be counted as not being up-todate. Assessing whether a person&acirc;&euro;&trade;s immunisations are up-to-date is primarily a clinical decision and we do not expect staff of social services departments who do not necessarily have relevant clinical training or access to the child&acirc;&euro;&trade;s medical records to make this decision on their own. For the purposes of the CRCS census an opinion from a doctor or practice nurse that a young person&acirc;&euro;&trade;s immunisations are up-to-date is sufficient. 1 = True; 0 = False.

This linkage process consists of matching against the Welsh Demographic Service by NHS number, where a valid number exists, and where there is no valid number then matching is attempted using first name, surname, date of birth, and postcode. This is an artificial score with no real-world meaning; i.e. a match of .99 does not mean there is a 99% chance the match is correct. This number is assigned when deriving the Encrypted Anonymised Linking Field.
